output.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, structure, containment/owner default-entry, transition-group guard collisions, wrong local-exit targets, and unauthorized edges by comparing NL contracts against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM. Most NL1-NL11 obligations are satisfied by exact matching source/model edges and containment. NL12/NL13 obligations concerning CollisionAvoidance are structurally present in the source and FCSTM (edges exist, states exist, containment exists), but the CollisionAvoidance owner composite has no default entry realized from root/top-level - it is a sibling composite of AutonomousMode never reached from the machine root, per inspection_equivalent_facts (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL, EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE) and verify_facts (reachability refuted for CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active; event-consumer refuted for both CollisionAvoidance events). This is a root-reachability defect for the CollisionAvoidance scope, not an initial_entry defect (the owner-local edge to collision_avoidance_deactive does exist, matching NL12-INITENTRY-1's owner-local requirement) and not itself a violation of the endpoint/guard contracts, which are locally exact. I therefore emit one derived reachability contract for CollisionAvoidance scope. I also keep the supplied NL12-DERIVED-94... event_consumer_coverage contract as a candidate reflecting narrower unreachable coverage of the pedestrian_detected disjunct. Also audited NL2 guard_disjointness: high_way=true and urban_way=true are disjoint predicates (mutually exclusive), so NL2-GUARDDISJ-1 is satisfied and omitted. NL1 containment and init-entry are satisfied (root->AutonomousMode->InitialState edges exist). NL3-NL11 endpoints, containments, guards all match exact source/FCSTM edges and are omitted as satisfied. NL6/NL10 termination checks: FinishState is reached by many transitions, but FinishState/HighwayMode/UrbanMode each exit to [*] under guard R45RouteToken==29, and the enclosing AutonomousMode itself has a self-transition AutonomousMode->AutonomousMode under the identical guard (line 90, diagnostic I_TRANSITION_TO_SELF_VIA_PARENT, crosses_composite=true), which structurally re-enters AutonomousMode's own initial edge back toward InitialState/HighwayMode instead of remaining terminated. This is flagged as a structural termination concern for both NL6 and NL10 per frontier discipline: a designated ending target that can cycle back into continued operating behavior is an independent termination defect even when the endpoint transition itself exists.

result.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, structure, containment/owner default-entry, transition-group guard collisions, wrong local-exit targets, and unauthorized edges by comparing NL contracts against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM. Most NL1-NL11 obligations are satisfied by exact matching source/model edges and containment. NL12/NL13 obligations concerning CollisionAvoidance are structurally present in the source and FCSTM (edges exist, states exist, containment exists), but the CollisionAvoidance owner composite has no default entry realized from root/top-level - it is a sibling composite of AutonomousMode never reached from the machine root, per inspection_equivalent_facts (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL, EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE) and verify_facts (reachability refuted for CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active; event-consumer refuted for both CollisionAvoidance events). This is a root-reachability defect for the CollisionAvoidance scope, not an initial_entry defect (the owner-local edge to collision_avoidance_deactive does exist, matching NL12-INITENTRY-1's owner-local requirement) and not itself a violation of the endpoint/guard contracts, which are locally exact. I therefore emit one derived reachability contract for CollisionAvoidance scope. I also keep the supplied NL12-DERIVED-94... event_consumer_coverage contract as a candidate reflecting narrower unreachable coverage of the pedestrian_detected disjunct. Also audited NL2 guard_disjointness: high_way=true and urban_way=true are disjoint predicates (mutually exclusive), so NL2-GUARDDISJ-1 is satisfied and omitted. NL1 containment and init-entry are satisfied (root->AutonomousMode->InitialState edges exist). NL3-NL11 endpoints, containments, guards all match exact source/FCSTM edges and are omitted as satisfied. NL6/NL10 termination checks: FinishState is reached by many transitions, but FinishState/HighwayMode/UrbanMode each exit to [*] under guard R45RouteToken==29, and the enclosing AutonomousMode itself has a self-transition AutonomousMode->AutonomousMode under the identical guard (line 90, diagnostic I_TRANSITION_TO_SELF_VIA_PARENT, crosses_composite=true), which structurally re-enters AutonomousMode's own initial edge back toward InitialState/HighwayMode instead of remaining terminated. This is flagged as a structural termination concern for both NL6 and NL10 per frontier discipline: a designated ending target that can cycle back into continued operating behavior is an independent termination defect even when the endpoint transition itself exists.

Event-consumer coverage obligations (i0, i3, i18) are established given exact deterministic event_consumer/verify_facts rows showing declared-but-unreachable consumers; declared-only existence is a weaker property and does not rebut the reachable-consumer coverage requirement. The termination obligation (i5) is established given the exact non-final continuation facts (tr_0024/tr_0029) contradicting a stable termination boundary at FinishState; no exact terminal edge or NL terminal clause supports an intentional-terminal rebuttal. The containment/FinishState-scope obligation (i19) is established from exact first-mention/cross-scope usage facts showing an inconsistency between declared containment and NL/source usage, with the strongest rebuttal (self-consistency of the closed model) not defeating the source-vs-model divergence itself. The three containment-frontier-unresolved obligations (i20, i21, i22) are genuinely unresolved: the deterministic frontier explicitly retained them without resolving to any closed-model identity, and no supplied fact permits a decision either way.

The one S5 obligation with a completed backend receipt (i14) is established by direct verdict=false. S2 endpoint-absence obligations with completed receipts (i23, i24) are established violations. G1 reachability obligations with completed receipts (i2, i4) establish unreachability of CollisionAvoidance as a first violation. The initial-entry obligation (i1) is a separate owner-local claim about the well-formed local edge into a scope that is itself unreachable; per the initial-entry-scope protocol this remains an established defect despite the local edge being present. Event-consumer coverage obligations (i0, i3, i18) are established given exact deterministic event_consumer/verify_facts rows showing declared-but-unreachable consumers; declared-only existence is a weaker property and does not rebut the reachable-consumer coverage requirement. The termination obligation (i5) is established given the exact non-final continuation facts (tr_0024/tr_0029) contradicting a stable termination boundary at FinishState; no exact terminal edge or NL terminal clause supports an intentional-terminal rebuttal. The containment/FinishState-scope obligation (i19) is established from exact first-mention/cross-scope usage facts showing an inconsistency between declared containment and NL/source usage, with the strongest rebuttal (self-consistency of the closed model) not defeating the source-vs-model divergence itself. branches.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, structure, containment/owner default-entry, transition-group guard collisions, wrong local-exit targets, and unauthorized edges by comparing NL contracts against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM. Most NL1-NL11 obligations are satisfied by exact matching source/model edges and containment. NL12/NL13 obligations concerning CollisionAvoidance are structurally present in the source and FCSTM (edges exist, states exist, containment exists), but the CollisionAvoidance owner composite has no default entry realized from root/top-level - it is a sibling composite of AutonomousMode never reached from the machine root, per inspection_equivalent_facts (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL, EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE) and verify_facts (reachability refuted for CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active; event-consumer refuted for both CollisionAvoidance events). This is a root-reachability defect for the CollisionAvoidance scope, not an initial_entry defect (the owner-local edge to collision_avoidance_deactive does exist, matching NL12-INITENTRY-1's owner-local requirement) and not itself a violation of the endpoint/guard contracts, which are locally exact. I therefore emit one derived reachability contract for CollisionAvoidance scope. I also keep the supplied NL12-DERIVED-94... event_consumer_coverage contract as a candidate reflecting narrower unreachable coverage of the pedestrian_detected disjunct. Also audited NL2 guard_disjointness: high_way=true and urban_way=true are disjoint predicates (mutually exclusive), so NL2-GUARDDISJ-1 is satisfied and omitted. NL1 containment and init-entry are satisfied (root->AutonomousMode->InitialState edges exist). NL3-NL11 endpoints, containments, guards all match exact source/FCSTM edges and are omitted as satisfied. NL6/NL10 termination checks: FinishState is reached by many transitions, but FinishState/HighwayMode/UrbanMode each exit to [*] under guard R45RouteToken==29, and the enclosing AutonomousMode itself has a self-transition AutonomousMode->AutonomousMode under the identical guard (line 90, diagnostic I_TRANSITION_TO_SELF_VIA_PARENT, crosses_composite=true), which structurally re-enters AutonomousMode's own initial edge back toward InitialState/HighwayMode instead of remaining terminated. This is flagged as a structural termination concern for both NL6 and NL10 per frontier discipline: a designated ending target that can cycle back into continued operating behavior is an independent termination defect even when the endpoint transition itself exists.
